notes: §1985:VII.3.8.2 prints RECORD CONTAINS integer-1 CHARACTERS, RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE [[FROM integer-2] [TO integer-3] CHARACTERS] [DEPENDING ON data-name-1], and 'RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5 CHARACTERS'; its integers are nonzero (§1985:III.2: 'must be neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed by the rules for that format') and only Format 2 relates its bounds (SR3, 'Integer-3 must be greater than integer-2'). recordClause parses the three formats in the printed sequence, BindRecordClause captures the integers and data-name-1, VisitRecordClause refuses BYTES at 85, and both departures of the prior PARTIAL read are closed on this tree: RecordClauseRules rows now carry Since and AppliesAt, so Format 3's 2002 ordering rule does not fire at 85 (RECORD CONTAINS 8 TO 8 CHARACTERS runs), and IntegerOperandPass.RecordClause refuses zero at 85 with the §1985:III.2 message (COBOL2386). Probed at --std 85: (b) zero in each of integer-1, integer-2 and integer-4, +8, FROM 8 TO 2 (COBOL2009), DEPENDING before FROM, DEPENDING on a CONTAINS form, the clause twice and a record longer than integer-3 (COBOL2010, SR2) are refused, and a signed DEPENDING item (COBOL2922, SR4); (c) BYTES refused COBOL0900; (a) RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 2 TO 8 DEPENDING ON WN over an ODO record writes 4 and 8 characters (00), a WRITE with WN = 1 gives 44, the READs set WN to 04 and 08 and R(1:WN) shows the records, a READ after CLOSE gives 47; DEPENDING ON GN OF G (qualified) writes 6 characters; Format 3 with two record sizes runs. The witness runs the three formats and a bare RECORD VARYING with unequal bounds and reads the records back. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5115 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5196 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09-refute.json).

next.reason: §1985:VII.3.8.2 has three RECORD formats ending in CHARACTERS: CONTAINS integer-1, IS VARYING IN SIZE, and CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5. §2023:13.18.43.2 keeps all three but offers BYTES beside CHARACTERS in each, and §2023:13.18.43.3 SR2 makes them synonyms ('The words BYTES and CHARACTERS are synonymous and may be used interchangeably'), so RECORD CONTAINS 80 BYTES, refused by the 1985 format, is accepted. 2023 also restricts the third format where 1985 does not: §2023:13.18.43.3 SR9, 'Integer-5 shall be greater than integer-4' (1985's only rule on them, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13, calls them the minimum and the maximum), so RECORD CONTAINS 80 TO 80 CHARACTERS, conforming in 1985, is refused. Wider and stricter at compile time, no exception condition: CHANGED.
